newsitem.title: FRANCE: French envoy to press Belgrade on elections.
newsitem.headline: French envoy to press Belgrade on elections.

text.p: France urged Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Thursday to acknowledge all opposition victories which he annulled following municipal elections in November.

The Foreign Ministry said an envoy was being sent to Belgrade to urge the Serbian government to heed confirmation of the victories by an internation mission headed by former Spanish Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez.

"It is essential today that the recommendations made by the personal representative of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, Felipe Gonzalez, be implemented fully and immediately," ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.

"The Serbian government must admit, unconditionally and without qualification, that the opposition was victorious in 15 Serbian cities including the capital, and in eight of Belgrade's districts" the spokesman told a news briefing.
He said it had been decided at a cabinet meeting on Wednesday to despatch Paul Poulade, director of continental Europe at the Foreign Ministry, to convey Paris's views to the Belgrade government.
Poulade would meet Serbian Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic and opposition leaders during his three-day visit beginning on Saturday.
Milosevic, under strong pressure from the United States and other countries, has made a concession to protesters by admitting that the opposition won elections in Serbia's second city of Nis.

But the opposition has vowed no letup in 52-day-old street demonstrations and Belgrade students planned a blockade on Thursday to test the will of police barring the path of their daily protest marches.
